MARKE.|105}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}} For leauing the commaundement of God, you hold the traditions of men, the vva{{ls}}hings of cru{{ls}}es and cuppes: & many other things you doe like to the{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}} And he {{ls}}aid to thē, Wel do you fru{{ls}}trate the precept of God, that you may ob{{ls}}erue your ovvne tradition. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}} For Moy{{ls}}es {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 12.''}}* ''Honour thy father & thy mother''. and, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 20, 9.''}}* ''He that {{ls}}hal cur{{ls}}e father or mother, dying let him dye''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}} But you {{ls}}ay, If a man {{ls}}ay to father or mother, ''Corban'' (vvhich is a {{sup|‖}} gift) vvhat{{ls}}oeuer proceedeth from me, {{ls}}hal profit thee: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}} and further you {{ls}}uffer him not to doe ought for his father or mother, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}} defeating the vvord of God for your ovvne tradition vvhich you haue giuen forth. and many other things of this {{ls}}ort you doe.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}} And calling againe the multitude vnto him, he {{ls}}aid to them, Heare me al you, and vnder{{ls}}tand. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}} {{sup|‖}} Nothing is vvithout a man entring into him, that can defile him. but the things that proceede from a man tho{{ls}}e are they that make a man {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the fir{{ls}}t annotation vpō this chapter.}}∷ cōmon. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}} If any man haue eares to heare, let him heare. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}} And vvhen he vvas entred into the hou{{ls}}e from the multitude, his Di{{ls}}ciples a{{ls}}ked him the parable. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}} And he {{ls}}aith to them, So are you al{{ls}}o vn{{ls}}kilful? Vnder{{ls}}tand you not that euery thing from vvithout, entring into a man, can not make him common: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}} becau{{ls}}e it entreth not into his hart, but goeth into the belly, and is ca{{ls}}t out into the priuy, purging al the meates? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}} But he {{ls}}aid that the things vvhich come forth from a man, they make a man common. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}} For from vvithin out of the hart of men proceede euil cogitations, aduouteries, fornications, murders, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}} theftes, auarices, vvickedne{{ls}}{{ls}}e, guile, impudicities, an euil eye, bla{{ls}}phemie, pride, foli{{ls}}hnes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}} Al the{{ls}}e euils proceede from vvithin, and make a man common.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}} And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 15, 21.''}}* ri{{ls}}ing from thence he vvent into the coa{{ls}}tes of Tyre and Sidon: and entring into a hou{{ls}}e, he vvould that no man {{ls}}hould knovv, and he could not be hid. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}} For a vvoman immediatly as {{ls}}he heard of him, vvho{{ls}}e daughter had an vncleane {{ls}}pirit, entred in, and fel dovvne at his feete. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}} For the vvoman vvas a Gentile, a Syrophaenician borne. And {{ls}}he be{{ls}}ought him that he vvould ca{{ls}}t forth the diuel out of her daughter. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=27}} Who {{ls}}aid to her, Suffer fir{{ls}}t the children to be filled. for it is not good to take the childrens bread, and ca{{ls}}t it to the dogges. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=28}} But {{ls}}he an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid to him, Yea lord. for the vvhelpes al{{ls}}o eate vnder the table of the<noinclude>{{continues|crummes}}</noinclude>
